newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moody's Thai downgrades discounted - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Moody's Thai downgrades discounted - analysts.

text.p: Analysts said on Wednesday that stock and money markets had largely discounted cuts by Moody's Investors Services of Thailand's long-term foreign currency debt as well as private bank debt and deposit ratings.

"I don't think we will see a market panic on the news. The negative impact would be fairly limited even though the downgrades will raise funding costs of financial institutions, especially when they go abroad," said Supawat Saichua of Krungthai Thanakit Plc.
However, a foreign analyst said that Moody's decisions could produce medium-term negative reaction in the market and from investors.
"They (Moody's) have given a lot of advance warnings ... but one consolation is that the downgrade (on government long-term debt) is only by one notch," said the analyst at Vickers Ballas and Co.
Moody's has downgraded the foreign currency ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Thailand to A3 from A2.
It also cut the senior debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to A3 from A2.
Moody's said the cuts reflected concerns over the asset quality of banks in Thailand and the instability of the country's entire financial system.

An analyst at Multi-Credit Corp of Thailand Plc said that Thai financial institutions had faced higher foreign funding costs since late last year after Moody's lowered Thai short-term debt ratings in October.
"The local market has been prepared for the news but (Moody's) timing was not that good. It comes as the baht eased to a near seven-year low against a strong dollar," he said.
But the analyst said the downgraded Thai ratings still kept the country within investment grades.
